picks.style: ancient greek chorus, lyre, aulos, frame drum, layered female voices, narrative, building dread
picks.why: The Judgement of Paris as choral myth — three goddesses bathing in mountain springs, Cassandra crying slay him, and Troy already doomed.

picks.style: greek tragic lament, solo female voice, plucked lyre, low drone, slow, keening
picks.why: Andromache's whole-length interrogation of her killer — what city have I betrayed, what house have I fired — closing on Hector dragged behind the chariot.

picks.style: antiphonal greek dirge, aged male voice answered by female chorus, bowed strings, frame drum, slow, desolate
picks.why: A true kommos: Peleus and chorus trading short lines of grief, call-and-response built for singing.

picks.style: greek tragic monody, solo male voice, rough lyre, sea-wind drone, bitter, rising
picks.why: The betrayed man addressing the cliffs and headlands as his only listeners — he is cutting down a corpse, the shadow of smoke, a mere phantom.

picks.style: ancient chorus, lyre, aulos, layered male voices, spare, wave-like, hushed
picks.why: Ten years of exile in one sustained choral image — no wine, no bread, only the arrow and the stagnant pool — then the turn toward homecoming.

picks.style: greek lament, aulos, low male voice with answering chorus, mournful, halting
picks.why: A man singing farewell to his bow as to a living friend torn from his hands.

picks.style: english pastoral air, baroque flute, viola da gamba, gentle tenor, unhurried, sunlit
picks.why: The pebbled stream, the bee humming fairy-tunes in praise of flowers, the rooks as cawing legislators debating in full senate — sustained and delighted throughout.

picks.style: georgian mock-heroic ode, harpsichord, baroque strings, arch tenor, courtly, drowsy
picks.why: A grand invocation to the goddess of idleness whose empire outspans Pekin and Agra — the joke is held elegantly across the whole passage.

picks.style: melancholy georgian air, harpsichord, muted strings, low baritone, languid, ironic
picks.why: Syren Sloth singing a dull quietus, the cloistered heart sitting squat at home like a pagod in a niche, closing on the barbed Such are thy comforts, blessed Solitude.

picks.style: baroque lament, ground bass, viol consort, soprano, slow, grieving
picks.why: A mother's refusal of spring itself — can all the rains that fall from weeping skies unlock the tomb — with the built-in refrain No, never, never.

picks.style: english baroque air, theorbo, recorder, clear soprano, tender, blooming
picks.why: From every tear that fell, a violet grew — grief turning into a flowerbed, and thence their sweetness came, and thence their mournful hue.

picks.style: baroque ode, trumpets, timpani, full chorus and organ, majestic, ceremonial
picks.why: Congreve's Hymn to Harmony, written to be sung, with the chorus line Confusion heard thy voice and fled already built into it.

picks.style: late roman stage recitation, plucked cithara, hand drum, dry baritone, clipped, wry, brisk
picks.why: Laconic Chilon complaining that his loins ache waiting for Solon to finish one saying in three hundred verses, then delivering Know yourself and refusing applause.

picks.style: late antique latin declamation, cithara, tambour, genial baritone, measured, even
picks.why: Measure is best, argued in a list that is already a refrain — of speaking, of being silent, of sleep, of waking — and ending let there be a measure.

picks.style: late antique latin recitative, lyre, low male voice, sea drone, oracular, unhurried
picks.why: The golden tripod drawn from the sea, passed around all seven sages and back, until Thales gives it to the god: no man should be believed wise, but a god.

picks.style: french mélodie, piano, warm mezzo-soprano, rubato, wintry, hushed
picks.why: The only candidate that is unbroken verse from end to end — the palm above the tombs, the doves scattering like a necklace coming unstrung, the soul as their nightly tree.

picks.style: roman declamatory ode, lyre, hand drum, resonant male voice, stately turning wry, measured
picks.why: Opens on the great Anchises charge — others will draw living faces out of marble, but you, Roman, spare the conquered and war down the proud — then drops into court epigram.

picks.style: victorian parlour ballad, upright piano, restrained baritone, spare, epigrammatic, rueful
picks.why: Only candidate in the work; carried by the Goldsmith line about a man who to party gave up what was meant for mankind.
